# `get_auto_load_calibration`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read whether calibration is loaded automatically.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | A |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, guider handler @0x77fd0 (64-bit build), MyDev::GetAutoLoadCalibration @0x93a70 |

Params are not consumed. Returns the cached auto-load-calibration flag as a boolean. No handler error. The method is registered in the guider command table (TCP 4400); a request that reaches the main imager and is relayed to the guider is a separate route with its own side effects, outside this entry's tier.

Side effects: None. Reads a cached device flag.

Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id).
